body.statement:
If \(f(a)=f_0\), \(\theta'(a)=r_0\), and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa_0\) are positive constants on \(J\), then
\[
 \mathcal V(P)=|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},
 \qquad
 T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
The spatial coordinate in \(\texttt{thm:causal-transfer}\) is affine with this image length. At any one fixed dose, translation and affine GCM equivariance reduce the canonical marginal to \(D(0)\). These identities do not imply a growing-domain excursion, observed-statistic transfer, or calibration theorem.
body.justification: Checks the constant-coefficient clock and fixed-location normalization exactly.
body.gap: The reduction supplies no growing-domain or calibration law.
body.consumer: It is a diagnostic identity only.
body.proof_tex:
Assume that \(f(a)=f_0\), \(\theta'(a)=r_0\), and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa_0\) on \(J\), where the three constants are positive.  Direct substitution into \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal V(P)
 &=\int_J\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}\,da
 =|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},\\
 T_n(P)
 &=n^{1/3}\mathcal V(P)
 =n^{1/3}|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The inverse local scale from \(\texttt{thm:causal-transfer}\) is constant in \(a\):
\[
 h_n(a)^{-1}=n^{1/3}
 \left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}. \tag{2}
\]
Integrating (2) from \(\inf J\) to \(a\) shows that \(\Psi_{n,P}\) is affine, and evaluating it at \(\sup J\) gives exactly the image length in (1).

For the fixed-location assertion, apply \(\texttt{lem:canonical-wellposedness}\) with \(m=1\), \(x_1=0\), and common shift \(r=x\).  Its finite-dimensional stationarity conclusion gives
\[
 D(x)\stackrel{d}{=}D(0). \tag{3}
\]
The proof of that lemma obtains (3) by translating the constraint and subtracting the affine tangent, which is precisely translation and affine GCM equivariance.  Equations (1)--(3) are constant-coefficient and fixed-location identities only; they imply neither a growing-domain excursion theorem nor statistical calibration.
